newsitem.title: USA: US, North Korea MIA talks end without progress.
newsitem.headline: US, North Korea MIA talks end without progress.

text.p: Talks between the United States and North Korea ended without an agreement to gain more information on Korean War servicemen missing in action for more than 44 years, the Pentagon announced Saturday.

"Despite assurances in advance of the talks with the North Koreans that we would deal conclusively with all issues, their delegation was unable to respond constructively to U.S. proposals," James Wold, leader of the United States delegation, said in a written statement.
The Korean War lasted from 1950 to 1953, but talks on recovering the remains of missing servicemen did not begin until 1996.

The latest weeklong talks ended on Friday evening in New York City without progress on the questions of live sightings of Americans allegedly living in North Korea, access to North Korea's military archives or the scheduling joint operations to recover the remains of Amerians buried in North Korea, Wold said.
Earlier Friday, the North Koreans met with some family members and veterans representatives to hear their concerns.

"This was the first time since the end of hostilities that a group of family members has been able t meet with North Korean officials who are responsible for the POW/MIA issue," the Pentagon said in a statement.
The negotiations were the fourth in the series that began in 1996. Talks one year ago resulted in a joint operation in North Korea that led to the return of remains of an American soldier.
But a second excavation scheduled for the fall of 1996 fell through after a North Korean submarine loaded with commandos ran aground last September off South Korea.
There are still some 8,100 U.S. troops missing from the Korean War. The Pentagon has said it has no evidence that any are being held captive in North Korea.
Talks in New York between the United States and South Korea to urge Pyongyang to begin four-way peace talks with China to negotiate a formal end to the 1950-53 Korean War broke off in April.

The concerns raised about servicemen missing in North Korea follow by some years similar concerns raised about service members missing in Vietnam. At one time, the question of missing servicemen in Vietnam was an explosive political issue, and delayed the resumption of diplomatic relations between Vietnam and the United States.

The first U.S. ambassador since the war arrived in Hanoi late this week and said he would continue to seek an accounting of service members missing there. But he also emphasised the interest of the United States in helping Vietnam to prosper.
